title: Why rate limits exist
subtitle: The turnstile, not the finish line.
takeaway: Rate limits control request traffic. Back off and retry later.

boards.heading: A fair entry rate
boards.note: Think of a turnstile at a busy venue.

boards.heading: Wait, then try again
boards.note: Follow Retry-After when it is provided.

boards.heading: Keep traffic steady
boards.note: Spread out requests. Avoid retry storms.

turns.speaker: student
turns.text: Pip, my app says too many requests. Did I break the internet?

turns.speaker: tutor
turns.text: Probably not. The service is limiting how quickly requests can arrive.

turns.speaker: student
turns.text: Like a bouncer outside a club?

turns.speaker: tutor
turns.text: More like a turnstile. It lets people through at a manageable pace.

turns.speaker: student
turns.text: So everybody gets a chance, and the room does not fill at once.

turns.speaker: tutor
turns.text: Exactly. Limits help protect capacity. Different services use different rules.

turns.speaker: student
turns.text: Should I keep pressing the button faster?

turns.speaker: tutor
turns.text: Please do not. A four twenty-nine response means too many requests.

turns.speaker: tutor
turns.text: Wait before retrying. Follow Retry-After if the response provides it.

turns.speaker: student
turns.text: And spread out the requests instead of sending one giant burst.

turns.speaker: tutor
turns.text: Yes. Add backoff, and avoid making every retry happen at the same instant.

turns.speaker: student
turns.text: The internet needs a queue. My coffee shop would understand.
